Subject: Cedarline Health — post-demo technical summary & decision matrix

Hi Sara / Tim,

Thanks again for the call earlier — appreciated the candid run-through of the decisioning pipeline and the SLA constraints. Per our discussion, I wanted to capture the technical highlights and a simple decision matrix so your infra + product teams have a single reference.

High-level goals we heard:
- Real-time claim triage: <200ms p95 for short text prompts (~512 tokens) at peak traffic
- Nightly bulk processing: high throughput for batched documents (1–5k reqs/min)
- Data control: logs retained for 90 days; no customer PII persisted in hosted logs

Key pain points discussed:
- Current vendor has unpredictable tail latency under bursts (observed >600ms p95)
- Cost blowups during month-end spikes
- Need for VPC/private deployment for PHI-sensitive workflows

Preliminary SLO targets you mentioned (for qualification):
- Online low-latency: 50–150ms p95 per token generation for 512-token requests (target 100ms p95)
- Throughput: sustained 120 req/s for the primary service with 2x burst allowance
- Availability: 99.9% for production endpoints

Model and topology considerations we covered:
- Preferred model class: 30–70B open LLM (ability to quantize to int8/int4)
- KV-cache and prefix caching important for repeated context across calls
- Routing: primary low-latency cluster + fallback to cost-optimized variant for degraded capacity
- Private deployment option (VPC) required for PHI; Dedicated pool for predictable throughput

Decision matrix (high level):
- Hosted (fastest TTV): good for non-PHI endpoints and early rollout; limited for 90-day retention
- Dedicated: matches throughput and latency SLOs with reserved capacity; recommended for prod triage service
- Private/VPC: required for PHI workflows and SOC2 controls; adds procurement timeline

Next steps (action items):
1) We’ll share a short capacity map (attached: Cedarline-MAP.xlsx) that maps expected qps, token mix, and instance sizing.
2) Karthik will scope quantization/throughput feasibility for your canonical prompt set — request: please drop 4 representative prompts + avg token lengths.
3) Grace will propose a 90-minute deep-ops session to go through network egress, KMS setup, and audit logs.
4) If the high-level SLOs look ok, we can sketch a canary plan for a 2-week pilot on Dedicated.

I’ve attached the MAP and a quick sketch of the SLO/topology we drew on the call (slo-topology-sketch.png). Please let me know if I missed or mischaracterized anything.

Thanks,

Thanks Michael — this looks right and is helpful. A couple clarifications from our infra side: 

- The 200ms p95 target was our current internal target; we are open to the 100ms p95 goal if achievable without major cost impact.
- For PHI paths, we need customer-managed keys (HSM preferred) and a formal audit trail for every inference request (who requested, which model, and which tenant).
- For bulk nightly jobs, token lengths average ~1,500 tokens (longer documents), and we estimate a peak batch window of ~6k/min for 45 minutes.

Action on our side: I’ll send over four example prompts and the long-doc batch sample by Friday. Also looping in our procurement lead (CC’d Tim) to get an initial sense of lead times for a Dedicated contract.

- Security: customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM) and request-level audit logs retained for 90 days

Proposed deep-ops agenda (90 minutes) — attendees: Cedarline infra + Redwood eng (Karthik), product ops (Grace):
1) Review prompt samples and token distributions (10 min)
2) Walk through Dedicated vs Private topology and network design (25 min)
3) Quantization and throughput expectations for 30–70B class models (20 min)
4) KV/prefix caching strategies and expected cache hit-rate impact on p95 (15 min)
5) KMS/HSM integration, audit log schema, and retention (15 min)

Before the call — what we need from you:
- Four representative short prompts and one long-doc batch sample (as Sara noted)
- A list of the top three tenant-sensitive fields that must never be stored in logs (so we can validate masking at the pipeline level)

Karthik will run a short feasibility pass on model quantization with your samples as soon as we have them; ETA two business days. Grace will send a calendar invite with a proposed time window (Mon/Tue next week).

If that matches your expectations, I’ll convert this into a short mutual action plan and we’ll kick the pilot scoping.
